Replace Synder's default invoice matching with a rule you define for this integration: which of your existing invoices Synder considers, and which one gets the payment.

Synder looks for an open invoice for the payment's customer, dated near the payment, and matches the invoice number when the payment carries one. You are about to replace exactly this. Nothing is pre-filled, so no existing configuration changes until you build a rule and save it.
What Synder does today, by default

Turn the rule on to build it. Switching it back off later returns this integration to the default matcher and your configuration, so re-enabling does not mean rebuilding it.
Synder's default matching stays in place.

Synder checks these against the invoices it found, so anything goes here — including the statement memo and “is not / is empty”, which QuickBooks cannot filter on. If several invoices match, Synder takes the one with the — and more than one match usually means the conditions are too loose.
Iteration 1 ships a single box with one AND/OR for the whole box. Nested groups and named presets are explicitly out of scope, so there is no “add group” control here.
The payment is bigger than the invoice still owes
puts the payment on the matched invoice anyway and leaves the difference as an overpayment. Turn it off and Synder cancels the sync instead. This only ever fires an invoice was matched.
No matching open invoice was found
On: nothing is created. Off: the payment is processed as usual. Same setting as the one in integration settings — .
Cancel sync if there is no matching open invoice found for a payment.

Synder searches your existing invoices and considers only the ones that belong to the same customer as the payment, and are dated within either side of the payment date, and have an invoice number that the payment's . They come back earliest invoice date first.
Out of those, it looks for the invoice where of these is true: If several invoices match, Synder takes the one with the earliest invoice date.
the payment's is equal to the invoice's
If it found one, the payment goes onto that invoice and . If the payment is bigger than what that invoice still owes, the difference stays as an overpayment.

If it found nothing — no candidates, or none of them qualified, or none of the conditions could be checked on this payment — the payment is processed as usual, as if no open invoice existed. Synder's default matching is tried as a fallback.

(Synder books these as a Sales Receipt) these are skipped, because the value they read does not exist: the invoice-number match (invoice number), condition 1 (invoice note). That is this rule checks — so simple charges will always fall through to “no open invoice found”. Add a row sourced from or if you need to catch them.

Synder searches your existing invoices and considers only the ones that belong to the same customer as the payment, and are dated within either side of the payment date, and have an invoice number that the payment's . They come back earliest invoice date first.
It applies the payment to the invoice on that list.
If it found one, the payment goes onto that invoice and . If the payment is bigger than what that invoice still owes, the difference stays as an overpayment.

If it found nothing — no candidates, or none of them qualified, or none of the conditions could be checked on this payment — the payment is processed as usual, as if no open invoice existed. Synder's default matching is tried as a fallback.
